name: Inbal Jerusalem Hotel
positioning: The Inbal: a neo-Byzantine hotel of Jerusalem stone in the Talbieh district, overlooking Liberty Bell Park
best_for: Travelers who want a balcony overlooking the Old City walls
Families wanting family rooms, connecting options and a toddler pool

facts.text: The hotel sits in a former olive grove in the Talbieh district, overlooking Liberty Bell Park.
The hotel is a neo-Byzantine landmark built of Jerusalem stone.
The hotel's new room collection blends elegant luxury with contemporary, warm design.
Rooms are decorated in muted cream and honey hues with marble and glass furnishings.
Accommodations include spacious family rooms and connecting options.
Premium rooms and suites come with exclusive access to the Executive Lounge.
The pool is framed by a border of tall green pines.
A separate toddler pool is available.
Both male and female spa therapists are available.
The concierge team offers insights into Jerusalem's cultural, historical and religious sites.
02 is the hotel's kosher chef meat restaurant.
Shabbat meals are served on Friday evening and at Saturday lunch.

highlights.text: Select rooms and suites have private balconies overlooking the Old City walls.
The hotel has a heated lap pool with a spacious sundeck, in use year-round.
The Inbal Spa, enriched by AHAVA, uses AHAVA's skincare line in its massage therapies and body treatments.
A live 360-degree panorama camera on the hotel's roof streams Jerusalem views around the clock.
The hotel celebrates Sukkot beneath a modern designed Sukkah.

considerations.text: The pool is open to the sky in summer and fully covered in winter.
WhataHotel notes that kosher dining rules may limit some culinary options.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Inbal Jerusalem Hotel
